hints.title: Track the approximation error
hints.body: Let T be the four-strip estimate and I the exact integral. An overestimate means T−I>0. Ask how reflection or subtracting the function from 1 changes both quantities.
hints.recap: Transform the error as well as the graph.
hints.pitfall: You do not know a and b, so avoid assuming one curvature sign throughout.

recall.reminder: Track signed trapezium error through scaling and added constants.

hints.title: Reflect the sampled inputs
hints.body: Compare <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>, and track what reflection does to the equal strip widths and the exact integral.
hints.recap: The trapezium estimate is built from the sampled heights and widths.
hints.pitfall: A reflected interval has its endpoints in the reverse order before relabelling.
hints.pause: Determine how reflection affects the approximation error.

recall.reminder: The trapezium estimate is built from the sampled heights and widths.

hints.title: Use a complementary function
hints.body: Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>. The trapezium rule is exact for the constant function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: Both the exact integral and trapezium sum are linear in the heights.
hints.pitfall: Compare approximation minus exact value, using the same sign convention throughout.
hints.pause: Express the new error in terms of the old one, then assess both statements.

recall.reminder: Both the exact integral and trapezium sum are linear in the heights.

solution:
Write I=∫absin2xdx and let T be its four-strip estimate, with T>I.

For I, sin2x is even. Reflection sends [a,b] to [−b,−a] and reproduces all four trapezia and the exact area, so the error stays T−I>0. Statement I is true.

For II, cos2x=1−sin2x. Its exact integral is (b−a)−I. The same four-strip trapezium rule is linear and exact for the constant 1, so its estimate is (b−a)−T. The new error is I−T<0, an underestimate. Statement II is true.

Answer D: I and II.
knowledgePattern: Preserve quadrature error under even reflection and reverse it under complementation
